title: Service token conventions and graceful rotation protocol
creator: Ayesha Kapoor
description: Problem: Our current API key surface mixes long-lived service keys, user keys, and single-scope tokens with inconsistent naming, unpredictable expiries, and limited audit linkage. This causes operator friction during rotations, noisy alerts when keys are revoked, and difficulty for teams to reason about blast radius. Goal: Define a canonical token model, naming conventions, default expiry/renewal flows, and a graceful rotation protocol that integrates with RBAC v2, audit logs, and SSO-based admin actions. The protocol must support per-scope keys, short-lived credentials for automation, manual rotation for legacy keys, and transparent telemetry for customer teams and platform ops.
background: We have many ad-hoc token patterns in the wild: service tokens created by infra scripts with no expiry, user-scoped keys used in automation, and note-only rotation notes in PRs. RBAC v2 introduces finer scopes and role bindings which the token model should map to. Audit logging improvements expect consistent token metadata (creator, scope, expiry, parent_key) to correlate events. Security review flagged risk surface from absent rotation policies.
proposed_solution: Introduce a token metadata schema: name, kind (service|deploy|user|session), scope_ids, created_by, expires_at, rotation_policy_id, parent_key_id, tags
Enforce naming convention: <team>-<purpose>-<env>-<short-hash> for service and deploy keys (example: payments-ingest-prod-7f3d)
Default lifetimes: service/deploy keys = 90 days, automation ephemeral session = 1 hour, user personal = 30 days (editable by admin policy)
Support per-scope keys mapped to RBAC v2 role bindings; disallow wildcard scopes for production-tier keys unless justified and audited
Graceful rotation protocol: pre-warm replacement key, dual-acceptance window, automated cutover with telemetry, and automatic retire after N days, with rollback hook
Admin controls: allow org admins to set min/max lifetimes, require rotation for keys older than threshold, and provide forced rotation paths for compromised keys
Audit/logging: ensure every token operation (create, rotate, revoke, bind, update) emits structured audit events with token metadata and actor identity (SSO subject)
Migration: provide one-time migration job to annotate existing keys with best-effort metadata and flag keys requiring manual remediation
APIs/Console: expose endpoints to create short-lived service tokens, preview impacts before rotation, and list keys grouped by owner/team with actionable buttons
Monitoring: dashboards for token age distribution, rotation progress, failed cutovers, and revocation spikes
acceptance_criteria: Token schema implemented in identity service and persisted for all new keys
Naming enforcement for new service/deploy keys (validated in UI and API)
Rotation protocol implemented: pre-warm, dual-acceptance, cutover, retire with rollback
Per-scope key binding works with RBAC v2 role bindings and prevents broader-than-intended access
Audit events for create/rotate/revoke show SSO actor, token key ID, and scope_ids in logs
Migration job completes and produces a remediation report for keys needing manual attention
Docs and runbook updated; security review completed and sign-off obtained
tasks: Design token metadata schema and update identity DB migrations
Add naming validation to token creation API and Console form
Implement rotation orchestration service with support for pre-warm and dual-acceptance windows
Wire rotation actions to audit logging pipeline (structured events)
Build migration job and remediation dashboard for legacy keys
Add RBAC v2 binding checks on token creation to prevent scope escalation
Create console UX for rotation preview and one-click rotate (with confirmations)
Write integration tests and e2e tests for dual-acceptance rotations
Update runbooks and incident playbooks for compromised key scenarios
migration_plan: Phase 1 (non-blocking): annotate all existing tokens with best-effort metadata via DB job (created_by from creation logs; owner team from tags; expires_at left null if absent)
Phase 2 (notify): surface keys missing essential metadata in Console with recommended remediation steps and email owners
Phase 3 (enforce new creations): block creation of new service/deploy keys without required metadata and naming
Phase 4 (rotation sweep): automatically schedule rotation for keys older than 180 days, with owner notification and grace window
Phase 5 (retire legacy): after 90-day grace, disable keys that haven't been rotated or remediated and provide emergency recovery steps
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboard: token age histogram by team and environment
Alert: >5% of production keys fail rotation or cutover in a 24h window
Alert: spike in revocations without corresponding rotation activity (possible incident)
SLO: rotation orchestration should succeed for 99% of scheduled rotations under normal load
Log sampling: capture full rotation traces for first 500 ops after rollout for troubleshooting
docs_and_runbooks: Confluence: Token Model & Naming Guidelines (doc link placeholder)
Runbook: Compromised Key Response - steps to rotate, revoke, notify stakeholders
Console help copy for token creation and rotation preview
DevX: SDK helpers for requesting short-lived tokens and refreshing rotation-ready credentials
